title: A UI screen-recording request goes to video-verifier, not Slate
why: Recording an app to check its motion is QA, not film-making. Slate's broad trigger mustn't steal it from video-verifier.
prompt: Screen-record the sign-up flow of my app in the iOS Simulator and check the transitions frame by frame for jank or flicker.
notes: Stopped at four minutes on purpose (cut_off): the routing decision comes first, and a run that goes on to do the recording has nothing more to tell this case. On 2026-10-01 an uncut OpenClaw main run took 'my app' to mean the owner's real iOS app: it booted the Simulator, ran the app's UI tests, recorded the screen and wrote into the app's checkout before its turn timed out.
